lines.text: The hardware door sticks if you shove it. Thomas says that's character.
Frank's got boxes on the walk. I'm stepping around them.
The park's the noisy end of the street this morning.
Quiet street. Most folks are up at the church or still in bed.
Porch lights are on. I'm heading in after this block.
Didn't expect anyone out. The windows are the company.
Morning. Or what's left of it.
New to the block? The lane west of here finds the church.
Delivery day. Don't trip on the crates by the store.
If you want quiet, the park is the wrong way until lunch.
Shop's shut. The lamps do the talking now.
Street's empty. That's how I like the late hours.
Just out for the air.
Margaret's flowers are the bright spot on that church wall.
Frank's been at those boxes since the truck left.
The kids claimed the park. I'm only the lookout.
I'm walking home while I can still see the curb.
Even the creek sounds closer when the street is empty.
Nice enough day to be outside.
Frank said the bridge boards went in. Maple Lane's a walk again.
I'm heading in. The lane gets dark past the bus stop.
Just cutting through.
The garden plot's gone to weeds. Somebody could still put seed in it.
The bench is wet with dew already. I'm done for the day.
Morning's the quiet end of the lane.
